messages.subject: [rkward-users] [Help] RE: Cannot save rkward configuration
messages.body_plain:
The following forum message was posted by tfry at http://sourceforge.net/projects/rkward/forums/forum/165574/topic/4598380:

Hi!

Settings should always be saved automatically on exit (unless RKWard crashes).
I suspect the problem might be that you do not have write permission to the
KDE settings folder inside your home directory. This can happen under some
circumstances, e.g. if you run KDE applications as root (esp. when using the
--preserve-environment option of su). Try running
[code]chown --recursive USERNAME:USERNAME ~/.kde[/code]
and then try again.

Let us know, if the problem persists after that.

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] rkward.frontend.exe stops working Windows installation
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

On Friday 08 July 2011, Sandy Elliott wrote:
> I have installed the bundled Windows binary
> RKWard-0.5.6_KDE-4.5.4_R-2.13.0_bundle on a Windows 7 machine but the
> interface is not working properly. Rkward opens fine, I can edit a new
> table, but I get rkward.frontend.exe stopped working error message when
> trying to save a new script. Similar messages or freezing when opening a
> previous workspace or setting the workspace. I have not installed R,
> Rkward, or KDE on this computer before. I have admin privileges. What
> should I try next?

hm, it looks like the common aspect of these freezes is that a file-selection 
dialog is (about to be) shown. So probably the problem is related to that.

On startup, RKWard prompts you about disabling "native file dialogs", unless 
you have already done so. Have you answered "Yes" to this question? *If* you 
have not, please do so the next time you start RKWard, and try again.

So far I have only heard of problems with "native file dialogs", but perhaps 
the "non-native" variant has problems on other systems. Thus, if you see this 
problem after you have disabled the native file dialogs, try the following:

1) Enter
    rk.sessionInfo()
in the R Console. Find the line that reads "Local KDE directory" and open the 
given folder in the Windows file browser. Exit RKWard.

2) Navigate to the sub-folder "share\config", and remove / rename "rkwardrc" 
(this resets all RKWard settings).

3) Start RKWard again. Answer "No", when prompted to disable native file 
dialogs. Try any of the problematic actions you listed.

Does that fix the problem for you?

Do you have any connected tape storage drives (this was know to cause problems 
in KDE on Windows in the past, although, I thought those were fixed in KDE 
4.5.4)? Are you aware of anything else that might be "unusual" about your 
setup?

Thanks!
Thomas

messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] command to open script file from Krusader
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Sunday 10 July 2011, Mihai Terente wrote:
> I'm trying to find a way to open a script file with Rkward from Krusader.
> If I give the default command, e.g. open with... it runs rkward
> -caption "%c" %i. This seems a command for opening workspaces and I
> think that's why I get this message into the Rward command log:

yes, in fact, RKWard will try to load this as a workspace (and fail). There 
simply is no command line option to open a script file, so far. Consider 
opening a wishlist item in our tracker 
(http://sourceforge.net/tracker/?atid=459010&group_id=50231&func=browse).

Here is a workaround of sorts:
  rkward --evaluate "file.edit (\"filename.r\")"
will open the script file (and bug you with a dialog).

Regards
Thomas

messages.body_plain:
hi sourav,

am Donnerstag 14 Juli 2011 (17:41) schrieb Sourav Chakraborty:
> It is giving me dependency error. I tried to install the dependencies
> one by one. But it did not work. The error codes were coming back in
> loop. I have attached the error codes here. Hope this will help explain
> the problem better.
> 
> Here are the pastebin files:
>       * http://paste.ubuntu.com/644178/

the important part:

<snip>
gcc -I/usr/share/R/include      -fpic  -std=gnu99 -O3 -pipe  -g -c Hmisc.c -o 
Hmisc.o
In file included from /usr/include/bits/errno.h:25,
                 from /usr/include/errno.h:36,
                 from Hmisc.h:5,
                 from Hmisc.c:1:
/usr/include/linux/errno.h:4:23: error: asm/errno.h: No such file or directory
</snip>

so the header file "asm/errno.h" cannot be found on your system, but is needed 
to compile the Hmisc package sources. it's not a file from an R package, so 
you can't fix it by installing other R packages. you need to find out which 
ubuntu package provides it. run this on a console:

 dpkg -S asm/errno.h

it will search for "asm/errno.h" in all available packages, and show you that 
it's found in the package linux-libc-dev and linux header packages. once 
you've installed what you need (e.g. "sudo aptitude install <package name>", 
i'd go for the linux-libc-dev package first), try the R installation again.

> On a second note, I have observed some libraries were present in
> multiple locations. Was there any default location where they should be
> present (such as /usr/lib/R/library)?

R can handle several library locations. this allows you to have your own 
package collection in your home directory so you don't need sudo. on a 
distribution like ubuntu with an advanced package management system i would 
always prefer to keep it this way, so you don't accidently overwrite files 
from an ubuntu package, or revert manual changes with the next package update 
without notice.

> Also, is there an easy to way to uninstall packages beside remove.packages
> () function in R?

you can manage most official/common packages by the debian/ubuntu package 
tools, i.e. (un)install them as .deb packages. try this on a console:

 aptitude search r- | grep "GNU R"

as for packages in your home folder, you can simply delete the folder with the 
package name and the package is gone, too...

> P.S. I am using Ubuntu 10.04 with kernel-2.6.38-10-generic, 2 GB RAM and
> intel 2.00 GHz processor.

for problems like this one, it's always helpful to know the R and RKWard 
version numbers as well. there's actually a special function for this, called 
"rk.sessionInfo()". you can call it in RKWard to generate all information the 
developers desire to know ;-)


viele gr??e :: m.eik

--
